column3: "I used a color hierarchy based on the rainbow and kept using it. I wanted to be consistent and have my partner adapt to me because (unless they didn't respond for long enough but they did) so they wouldn't be confused if I kept changing by trying to adapt to them (in the event that they were also trying to figure out my system) it went pink (in place of red in the rainbow), orange, yellow, blue, indigo, purple, brown. So brown would never be chosen, pink would always be chosen if on the screen. Once the system was in place  I did not want to change anything. I went with this order as opposed to something like brightness levels because this is subjective and can be remembered easily by going through the rainbow so it can be checked if unsure."

"I analyzed what colors my partner and I were choosing and we were able to establish a hierarchy of colors based on that. We had an order of colors (pink, orange, yellow, light blue, dark blue, purple, and then brown) and whichever was higher between the two we would choose. For example between pink and dark blue we chose pink. I paid attention to what my partner was choosing and treid to adjust accordingly and notice patterns. At first I just picked randomly until we could develop a pattern. It took longer to develop the pattern becuase we couldn't communicate but by paying attention and recognizing patterns that helped the most."
